qualification: Local uncommitted experiment and paper update. No exact-commit remote CI, independent deployment, release or breakthrough qualification.
limits: Both gates share the kernel host, native scope verifier, graph adapter and courier. This compares outcome gate behavior in the graph, not two complete protocols.
Receiver keys, stores and processes are separate. Same-user filesystem access is not isolated, and no remote administrative or transport boundary is qualified.
The workload uses a static native capability policy and a fixed logical clock. It executes no live model or arbitrary proposed code.
A public test ingress issues receiver-signed exact-operation capabilities. No production identity system is evaluated.
Completed results are retrievable after response loss. Claimed effects without results remain uncertain and supply no successor evidence, even when their physical effect count is zero.
Receiver kills occur inside actual kernel tool evaluation. Recovery status receipts attest retrieval of stored results, not reconstruction of missing original invocation receipts.
The standalone executable was retained after implementation. The later added integration wrapper reran the entire graph and original local comparison; final all-target Clippy covers both tests.
Raw logs and owner/public configuration are retained; private seeds and binary databases are excluded. Source hashes describe the current uncommitted tree, not a remotely qualified commit.
No latency, integration-cost, storage-cost or deployment advantage was measured. The ordinary ledger matches the observed outcomes.
